title: Safe dependency wave and adaptive API compatibility layer
creator: Ava Patel
description: Scope: coordinate a cross-language dependency upgrade wave (Python, JS, Go) and introduce an adaptive API compatibility layer that allows us to stage deprecations without breaking customer code. Goals: 1) upgrade critical transitive deps (cryptography, http libraries, protobuf) to supported major versions with minimal runtime disruptions; 2) implement a lightweight compatibility adapter that provides runtime feature flags and shimmed call signatures for 3 months post-release; 3) remove legacy optional parameters from the public SDK surface after gradual rollout and telemetry validation; 4) improve client cold-start and tokenization path performance by lazy-initializing heavy modules and reducing synchronous work in constructors.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Ava Patel: Initial ticket. Drafted scope with PM and Design input. Identified high-risk deps: cryptography (py), golang.org/x/crypto, axios/httpx. Linked playbook and proposed rollout windows. Estimated 5 points for coordinated wave and compatibility layer implementation.

2026-03-01 - Liam Chen: Spike completed for Python: upgraded cryptography to 40.x in a feature branch and validated wheel compatibility across supported Linux distros. Found one incompatibility with our embedded TLS util; added small wrapper to preserve the old API surface. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234.

2026-03-04 - QA: Added test plan to run consumer integration suite against instrumented canary builds. Noted two flaky tests around client telemetry initialization; created follow-up ENG-531121 to stabilize telemetry lazy init.

2026-03-07 - Liam Chen: Prototype of the adaptive compatibility layer merged to monorepo alpha. Layer exposes runtime opt-in feature flags via environment and supports per-route shim mapping. Implementation uses thin runtime adapters to avoid extra allocations in tight loops. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/889.

2026-03-09 - PM review (Diego Ruiz): Approved phased rollout plan. Phase 1: library dep bumps and compatibility layer behind feature flag; Phase 2: enable for internal customers and monitor; Phase 3: public opt-in; Phase 4: finalize removal of legacy params after 90 days of stable telemetry.

2026-03-12 - Performance: Microbenchmarks show client cold-start improved ~18% after lazy imports and serialized KV cache deserialization. Added a note to acceptance criteria to include a perf gate. Perf board: https://dash.redwood.ai/boards/sdk-startup-latency
acceptance_criteria: All three language clients (Python/JS/Go) have major security/compat dependencies upgraded and release candidates published to our internal registry.
Adaptive compatibility layer exists behind a feature flag and can be toggled per-deployment without code changes.
End-to-end integration smoke tests pass for the canonical customer templates; no regressions in generation latency >5% P90.
Telemetry demonstrates stable behavior for 14 days on internal canaries and no customer-facing errors attributed to the upgrades.
Documentation updated: migrations guide, changelog, and deprecation notices. Public SDK changelog published on release page.
